title: Generic dichotomy for geometrically irreducible fibres on a closed irreducible subset
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $t\in Y$, let $X_t$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre over the residue field $\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $Z\subseteq |Y|$ be a nonempty irreducible closed subset [def-weil-irreducible-components]. There exists a nonempty relatively open subset $V\subseteq Z$ such that precisely one of the following alternatives holds:
$$\text{for every }t\in V,\ X_t\text{ is geometrically irreducible over }\kappa(t);$$
$$\text{for every }t\in V,\ X_t\text{ is not geometrically irreducible over }\kappa(t).$$
Geometric irreducibility means irreducibility and nonemptiness after every field extension [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Empty fibres belong to the second alternative. Neither flatness nor Noetherian hypotheses on $X$, $Y$ or $f$ are assumed.

source.place: Tag 055B (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-constructible), second paragraph at the level n=1, using Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good). This extracts old steps 3--4 up to the application of the Noetherian constructibility criterion.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], choose the generic point $\eta\in Z$, so $Z=\overline{\{\eta\}}$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-component-count-generic-constancy] to the given finite type $f$ and this point. It gives a nonempty relatively open $V\subseteq Z$ and $n\geq0$ such that, for every $t\in V$, the scheme $W_t=X_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t)^s$ has exactly $n$ irreducible components. Use the separable closures fixed in [def-pd-separable-closure]; in particular each $\kappa(t)^s$ is separably closed. No change of the base scheme or extra hypothesis on it is needed.

source.place: Tag 055B (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-constructible), second paragraph, applying Tag 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good); Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: For any topological space $W$, exactly one irreducible component is equivalent to irreducibility and nonemptiness. Indeed [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] says the components cover $W$. If there is exactly one, say $C$, then $W=C$, and $C$ is irreducible and nonempty by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Conversely, if $W$ is irreducible and nonempty, it is itself a maximal irreducible subset; any component contained in $W$ equals $W$ by maximality. Thus it is the unique component. This argument also checks that the empty space has zero components.

source.place: Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible), part (4), and the definition of an irreducible component.

proof.text: Fix $t\in V$. If $X_t$ is geometrically irreducible, [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] applied to $\kappa(t)^s/\kappa(t)$ makes $W_t$ irreducible and nonempty. Conversely, if $W_t$ is irreducible and nonempty, apply [lem-sbc-subset-geometric-irreducibility] with $k=\kappa(t)$, $\Omega=\kappa(t)^s$, the structure morphism of $X_t$, and $A=|X_t|$. The inverse image of this full subset is the full base-changed space. Hence that lemma makes $X_t\times_k E$ irreducible and nonempty for every field extension $E/k$, exactly geometric irreducibility by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Together with Step 2, this proves $X_t$ geometrically irreducible if and only if $n=1$.

If $n=1$, Step 3 gives geometric irreducibility for every $t\in V$. If $n\ne1$, Step 3 gives its failure for every $t\in V$. These alternatives cannot both hold, since $V$ is nonempty: choose a point of $V$ and the two conclusions contradict each other there. In particular an empty fibre has zero components by Step 2 and is never put in the first alternative. This proves precisely the stated dichotomy.
